text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > .audit/design-sol.md <<'EOF'
# Problem

Verify actual Rust company identity policy without compiling the application's async, SQLx and Polars graph or silently replacing the resolver with a mathematical imitation. The owned policy is `identity.rs`: `company`, `kind`, `expanded_edges`, `Components::{new,apply,outcomes}` and `resolve`. Existing tests establish competing-anchor review, explicit-kind exclusion and company identifier precedence. Parent/child payment attribution is separate; no new hierarchy semantics belong in this design.

# Usage (caller's view)

Proposed repository command:

```sh
./verification/identity/check.sh
./verification/identity/check.sh --harness competing_anchors
./verification/identity/check.sh --mutations
```

The default command runs every harness and fails on failed assertions, unsupported operations, insufficient unwinding or missing harnesses. Mutation mode temporarily edits real production `identity.rs`, runs its designated harness, requires an assertion counterexample, restores the source and reruns the clean suite. Compilation failures do not count as mutation detection.

The project-local `.agents/skills/verify-identity/SKILL.md` documents this one command, the source boundary, exact fixture domains and current successful bounds. It instructs maintainers to report counterexamples without adjusting production semantics to satisfy a proof.

# Shape

Recommend a standalone minimal Rust verification crate that **includes unchanged production `identity.rs` by path**, plus an explicitly described boundary adapter. No copied resolver and no production extraction initially.

```text
verification/identity/
  Cargo.toml          # isolated workspace, only required lightweight dependencies
  src/lib.rs          # adapter namespace and #[path] production inclusion
  src/fixtures.rs     # bounded symbolic choices -> concrete boundary inputs
  src/proofs.rs       # public resolve harnesses and independent assertions
  check.sh            # pinned Kani invocation, fail-closed result handling
  mutations.py       # isolated edits, restoration, expected counterexamples
.agents/skills/verify-identity/SKILL.md
```

Illustrative signatures, with proof-only types private:

```rust
struct SmallCase { kinds: [KindFixture; 4], companies: [CompanyFixture; 4], edges: u8 }
enum KindFixture { Missing, Company, Person, Organisation, Unrecognized }
enum CompanyFixture { Missing, First, Second, LowercaseFirst, Invalid }
fn concrete(case: SmallCase) -> (ResolutionInput, ScoringInput, Vec<ScoredPair>);
fn run(case: SmallCase) -> (Vec<ObservationResolution>, Vec<PairDecision>);
#[kani::proof]
fn competing_anchors();
#[kani::proof]
fn identifier_precedence();
#[kani::proof]
fn component_kind_conflict();
```

These enums describe test fixtures only; they do not become alternate production kind parsers. `run` calls included `identity::resolve`. The adapter supplies precisely the fields and operations consumed by that file, using real canonical types wherever lightweight inclusion permits. Any substitute ID wrapper must preserve ordering, equality and `as_str`; substitute input structs must match consumed fields. Canonical outcome/reason enums should be imported from source if practical. Otherwise report explicit structural adapter assumptions and add a source compatibility audit; do not claim whole-application type integration. Adapter `company`, `kind`, edge classification or component behavior is prohibited.

The public command hides harness orchestration; fixtures expose input bounds rather than internal stages. Production retains sole ownership of domain rules (boundary-discipline and single source of truth). Proof assertions derive expectations from independently selected fixture labels, never by calling `company` to define expected company acceptance.

Pseudocode:

```text
symbolically choose fixture tags and edge subset within declared bounds
construct unique ordered IDs, valid profile references and finite score values
call real resolve through included identity.rs
assert exact outcome IDs, basis and decision reasons for designated scenarios
assert at most one accepted company label per final identity component
assert explicit person and explicit organisation never share a component
```

# Properties and bounds

Start with separate small harnesses rather than one huge product:

* Parser: symbolic eight-byte ASCII identifiers, bounded ASCII surrounding whitespace, explicit length cases 0/7/8/9, digit-free rejection, punctuation and lowercase normalization. Explicit non-company kind excludes an otherwise valid identifier; missing kind permits it. State that Unicode and arbitrary lengths are outside this proof.
* Three observations: two distinct accepted anchors and an unanchored observation linked to both must preserve distinct anchor identities; both attachments remain Review with `CompetingCompanyAnchors`.
* Four observations: two unanchored observations form a connected group between distinct anchors. Verify group-wide competing-anchor review. Add the existing indirect-chain scenario.
* Three observations: unknown joins person then organisation, covering component-level conflict separately from immediate pair classification. An eligible direct person/organisation pair is Rejected with `PersonOrganisationConflict`.
* Seeded equal numbers coalesce without scored edges. Anchored components use `source-reported:companies-house:<number>` even when an observation has no name. Captured reporters retain `SourceReportedCompany`; attached observations retain inferred basis. Unanchored named singleton uses run-local ID; unnamed singleton is unresolved.

Graph harnesses use at most four observations, six unique observation edges, fixed short names/addresses and finite score fixtures below/at/above 0.999. Profile expansion must include one repeated-profile case and its budget-error branch to cover `expanded_edges`; direct construction of `CandidateEdges` alone would miss those mutations. Unwind values are discovered with unwinding assertions enabled and recorded per harness; observation count is not a sufficient unwind bound for string/library internals.

# Alternatives considered

A narrow pure-domain extraction would move the entire identity algorithm and its input/output vocabulary into a dependency-light shared module consumed by production and Kani. It offers stronger type fidelity and avoids adapter drift, but requires changing production ownership and callers. Extracting only conflict predicates leaves precedence, grouping and outcomes unverified. Even full extraction cannot honestly catch mutations left in production `identity.rs` adapters unless end-to-end inclusion harnesses remain. This exceeds the presently authorized small verification addition; reconsider only if unchanged-source inclusion demonstrably fails.

# Tradeoffs and feasibility risks

Kani 0.68.0 availability is not proof of Apple Silicon installability or usable CBMC/toolchain support. Confirm supported execution architecture before promising a run; use a documented supported Linux environment if needed. Standard-library BTreeMap/BTreeSet, allocation, formatting, Unicode helpers and floating-point comparisons may cause unsupported operations or excessive verification cost even with bounded fixtures. Stub none of these silently. Failure here is an integration blocker, not a verified result.

Mutation probes must independently remove the component conflict guard, disable competing-anchor review, allow explicit persons to anchor, break equal-number seeding and replace company-first outcomes with run-local identity. Each designated proof must fail on real changed source. Preserve and compare source hashes, reject preexisting dirty target files, restore in a finally/trap path, and verify clean rerun. Finite fixture proofs remain bounded, not arbitrary-input correctness.

# Synthesis decision and reconciliation

Candidate recommendation: unchanged-source inclusion first. No implementation or accepted deviations yet. The next step is a single compile/verify feasibility spike exercising production `resolve`; user clarification only affects whether separate attribution proofs are subsequently requested.
